title: Why attention is O(n^2), and what Flash and Sage change
hook: Score every token against every token and the table grows with the square. Slicing and online softmax hold less of it at once, with the same answer. Low precision is a different bargain.

verified.claim: attention_basic builds a full score matrix with einsum and then applies softmax.
attention_split works out how much it needs, splits the queries into slices when that exceeds free memory, and scores each slice in turn.
The backend is chosen at import in this order: sage, flash, xformers, pytorch, then split or sub-quadratic. Comfy Kitchen overrides it when its flag is set.
The CUDA flash backend of scaled_dot_product_attention is enabled when pytorch attention is on.
Slicing queries and online softmax match the full calculation to rounding error, and rounding Q and K to int8 does not.
The FlashAttention title calls it exact and the SageAttention title calls it 8-bit.
The graph ran on a CPU.

unchecked: We did not measure Sage or FlashAttention on a GPU, so we make no claim here about their speed or memory on your card.
The lab's int8 row is our own toy. SageAttention's real method, including what it quantizes and how it keeps accuracy, is not reproduced.
Which PyTorch backend runs for a given shape is decided inside PyTorch. We read only what ComfyUI turns on.
What the Comfy Kitchen attention does internally lives in another package we did not read.
